newsitem.title: HONG KONG: First Shanghai surges on red-chip demand.
newsitem.headline: First Shanghai surges on red-chip demand.

text.p: Shares of First Shanghai Investments Ltd rose on rotational buying for red-chip stocks, despite a potential dilution effect from possible implementation of share options proposed by its parent, brokers said.

"Investors were buying the stock because the company name includes the word Shanghai," said a sales director at a regional brokerage. "Rotational demand for red-chip stocks had made it (First Shanghai) one of the hottest despite dilution."
The shares gained HK$0.37 or 28.24 percent to HK$1.68 at midday on volume of 161.84 million shares worth HK$272.04 million.
Brokers said speculation that First Shanghai's parent may inject assets into the company in exchange for an increased stake fueled hope of stronger earnings base.

First Shanghai said its controlling shareholder, International Enterprises Investment Co Ltd, proposed share options to subscribe for First Shanghai shares which would have a dilution effect on shareholders' interest in the company.
